name: Amira Kowalski

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a field researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential, including anything you would not say in public. What does a normal working day look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the carpenters fitting stairs and timber screens in new apartment buildings. I'm fifty-eight, with a vocational trade certificate and a good lead carpenter's wage; I still like getting the last tread quiet under my boot. Every day I use an AI tool to sort delivery notes, then check the timber against the actual drawing. My partner Daniel and I have grown children, our home paid for and about ten months of expenses saved.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is wearing you out, and what keeps you interested?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Carrying stair sections upstairs wears me out, though the crew shares the heavy bits. Solving a crooked landing keeps me interested, and there are plenty of other builders nearby if I need different work. Daniel repairs musical instruments from home, so we do not rely entirely on my wage. I would like to finish regular site work at sixty-five if our savings and later income cover it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew a useful delivery list is still a useful delivery list, even if AI never does much more. A quiet stair is better advertising than a clever computer demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I would be comfortable with that picture. My wage is good, Daniel has his repair customers, and our ten-month reserve gives us time if a builder delays the next job. I would keep the sixty-five target rather than find a new worry to fill the space.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would keep leading the stair installations and checking the delivery notes as I already do. Over the next year I would set aside two paid hours a fortnight for the apprentice to practise setting out a stair with me, after agreeing that time with the builder. I would leave our existing savings payment unchanged.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, with a little disappointment because I enjoy trying a useful tool. My own work and our household money look secure in this picture.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the apprentice first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would lay out a short practice flight on spare timber before we cut the real string, the sloping piece supporting the steps. One wrong rise can make every step feel awkward.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who pays for those practice hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the builder to put the two hours on the paid rota. If that is refused, I would keep teaching during the ordinary paid fitting work rather than promise the apprentice unpaid evenings.

say: I would value **useful delivery lists** without expecting a revolution in stair fitting.
I would tell the crew **quiet stairs** still matter more than computer demonstrations.
think: Our **ten-month reserve**, good wage and Daniel's customers make ordinary site delays manageable.
I can keep the **sixty-five target** if our household figures continue to support it.
do: Keep leading **stair installations** and checking existing AI delivery notes against drawings.
Arrange two **paid practice hours** fortnightly for the apprentice only with the builder's agreement.
feel: I feel **calm** because work and household money look secure, though limited AI progress would disappoint me.
S0.quote: A quiet stair is better advertising than a clever computer demonstration.
fieldNote: Her **existing AI use** continues rather than becoming a new learning commitment.
The apprentice practice depends on **paid time**; she otherwise teaches during ordinary fitting work.

steps.text: Keep leading stair installations and checking existing AI delivery notes
Arrange fortnightly apprentice stair practice only if builder agrees two paid hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say faster ordering could spare us a van full of timber for the wrong landing. I would try the new tools, but I would not tell the apprentice a shorter office list proves a shorter site day is safe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own pay looks fairly safe because I can fit difficult stairs and plenty of local builders need that skill. Daniel's repair customers could spend less if their desk jobs shrink, so our household income could still fall. I support firms competing on price, but a family has to count what actually comes in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would ask for access to the builder's new AI delivery-matching feature and learn it on paid time using one completed stair order. In the first year I would compare its suggested quantities with the signed drawing before using it on a live delivery. If Daniel's takings fell for three months, we would postpone replacing our sound kitchen cupboards.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about Daniel's income rather than my next stair. Ten months saved and my wage give us choices, but I would notice fewer repairs going through his workshop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the new feature worth learning?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would give it the delivery notes from a stair we have already finished and see whether it spots the missing oak nosing, the strip at the step edge. If the builder will not give paid access, I will keep my current checked method.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would trigger postponing the cupboards?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Daniel and I would compare three months of actual takings with the same regular household costs. One quiet afternoon would not change the kitchen plan, but three weaker months would.

say: I would test **AI delivery matching** without assuming faster office work makes safe fitting faster.
I would keep the **apprentice's site time** visible when the builder sets targets.
think: My **stair skills** and plentiful local builders make my own wage look fairly secure.
Daniel's **repair income** could fall if customers lose desk work, despite our substantial reserve.
do: Learn the new **AI delivery feature** only with builder access and paid practice time.
Postpone **kitchen cupboards** only after Daniel's repair takings fall for three months.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible household income reduction, with savings and my own wage providing control.
S1.quote: One quiet afternoon would not change the kitchen plan, but three weaker months would.
fieldNote: She separates **secure trade pay** from a possible loss of her partner's customer income.
Her new learning is a specific **delivery feature**, not a relabelled check of existing software.

steps.text: Learn new AI delivery matching only with paid builder access using a completed stair order
Postpone kitchen cupboards only after three months of lower partner repair takings

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew the office could change in 2028 while capable robots reach stair fitting around 2031. I would rather learn what the machines actually do than forbid the apprentice from touching a screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty when thinking AI arrives and sixty-three when the capable robots follow. Losing stair wages at sixty-three could interrupt the last two years before my target, while Daniel's customers might cut spending earlier. Our house and savings make that manageable for a while, but they do not make two lost incomes imaginary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would request a paid supervised robot demonstration on a spare stair flight, with a fenced test area and a reachable stop control. I would keep paid stair shifts after 2028, and if my paid days fell for two months I would apply to posted local refurbishment jobs with safe lifting duties and pay covering our household gap. I would not buy a robot or assume the builder has offered me a trial place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, because the end of my earning plan could get squeezed from both sides. I still have savings, skills and other builders to approach, so I am not without a plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you bring retirement forward?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on the information I have today. I would compare the cost of stopping with taking another two years of safe paid work; I am not choosing an earlier exit in advance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you require before joining the demonstration?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The builder would have to offer me a paid supervised place, keep workers outside the fenced area during movement and prove the stop control works. Asking for a demonstration does not put my name on a trial crew.

say: I would distinguish **2028 office changes** from capable stair-fitting robots around 2031.
I would favour **paid demonstrations** rather than banning unfamiliar tools from the site.
think: Robots at **sixty-three** could interrupt the final two wage years before my retirement target.
Daniel's **repair takings** could weaken earlier, leaving two possible income gaps despite our savings.
do: Request a **paid supervised demonstration** with a spare flight, fenced area and reachable stop control.
Keep **paid stair shifts** after 2028 while offered.
Apply after two shorter months to **local refurbishment postings** only with safe lifting and gap-covering pay.
feel: I feel **anxious** about lost household income, while savings and local jobs leave me practical choices.
S2.quote: Asking for a demonstration does not put my name on a trial crew.
fieldNote: She does not confuse **requesting a demonstration** with joining an offered paid trial.
Her possible **job search** has a two-month trigger and retains local, safe-duty and sufficient-pay conditions.

steps.text: Request paid supervised spare-stair robot demonstration with fencing and reachable stop control
Keep paid stair shifts after 2028 while offered
Apply after two shorter months to posted local refurbishment jobs with safe lifting and gap-covering pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew five years is enough to test new planning tools carefully, with capable robots following around 2034. I would still put an apprentice beside a real stair instead of teaching only through pictures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AI would arrive when I am sixty-three and robots when I am sixty-six. My target is still sixty-five, so the physical machines could follow my departure if our budget works. Daniel's earlier customer risk still matters, but we have time to check the actual figures before changing the target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would learn the builder's new AI drawing-comparison feature on paid time if access is provided, checking it against stairs already installed. I would keep paid fitting shifts after 2031 if I am still working. Daniel and I would review our figures every autumn; if we need wages beyond sixty-five, I would apply to posted local site-checking roles only with manageable duties and pay covering that gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the possible household shortfall, but less rushed than in the 2028 picture. I can prepare without treating a target retirement date as money already in the bank.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a site-checking job suitable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want the posted hours, lifting requirements and wage before applying. I would not swap a good stair wage for a title that pays less than the gap in our household figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the apprentice learn from a drawing comparison?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show a changed landing level on the screen, then take the apprentice to measure the finished floor. A computer can flag a changed line without knowing whose boots will trip on the step.

say: I would use five years for **tested planning tools** before capable building robots around 2034.
I would keep **real stair measurements** in an apprentice's learning alongside screen comparisons.
think: My **sixty-five target** could precede capable robots, provided our household budget permits stopping.
Daniel's **customer income** remains a possible earlier loss, so the longer warning still requires planning.
do: Learn new **AI drawing comparison** only with paid builder access and completed stairs for checking.
Keep **paid fitting shifts** after 2031 if still working.
Apply to **local site-checking postings** only if wages are needed beyond sixty-five, duties fit and pay covers the gap.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible income shortfall, with more time to test tools and compare household figures.
S3.quote: A computer can flag a changed line without knowing whose boots will trip on the step.
fieldNote: Her **retirement target** is conditional, not an early exit triggered by the card.
She plans specific **new software learning** while keeping any later job search tied to an actual household shortfall.

steps.text: Learn new AI drawing comparison only with paid builder access on completed stairs
Keep paid fitting shifts after 2031 if still working
Apply if wages needed beyond sixty-five to posted local manageable site-checking jobs with gap-covering pay

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew a decade gives us time to pass on good stair work before thinking AI in 2036 and capable robots around 2039. I would not promise every apprentice that one trade will last unchanged for life.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be sixty-eight at the thinking date and seventy-one when the robots follow. If our finances allow the sixty-five plan, I expect to be out of paid site work before either. I have enough savings and good earning options now that my own household looks secure in this longer picture, even though I cannot guarantee investment returns or Daniel's future customers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Starting now I would keep paid stair work and record one awkward landing measurement each month for the apprentice during paid site time. Daniel and I would keep our existing savings plan and check annually whether sixty-five remains affordable. In the year after 2036 I would stay off the paid rota if retired; if we still needed wages, I would apply only to posted local part-time checking work with safe duties and pay filling our budget gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about my own living in this picture, because the time and our existing position give the plan room. I would still care about the younger crew's prospects, but that is different from fearing my next bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does the card itself make you stop earlier?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, sixty-five was my target before you read any cards. I would move the date only when the household figures or my health justified doing so.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which measurement would you leave the apprentice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would record the finished floor level as well as the bare landing, because a later floor layer can change the final step. A stair starts with the floor people will actually walk on.

say: I would use the **decade** to pass on stair knowledge without promising an unchanged lifetime trade.
I would keep **finished floor levels** in the apprentice's records before future machines arrive.
think: Our **existing resources** and earning options make retirement before 2036 look affordable if the plan holds.
At **sixty-eight**, I expect to be off site; any further paid work depends on an actual household gap.
do: Keep **paid stair work** and record a difficult landing measurement monthly for the apprentice.
Review the existing **sixty-five plan** annually without claiming new saving or an earlier exit.
Apply after 2036 to **local part-time checking** only if wages remain needed, duties are safe and pay fills the gap.
feel: I feel **calm** about my household, while caring about the younger crew's uncertain future.
S4.quote: A stair starts with the floor people will actually walk on.
fieldNote: Her calm rests on **resources and time**, rather than a promised retirement payment or immunity from change.
The **post-2036 job search** is a fallback; she otherwise expects her original retirement target to hold.

steps.text: Keep paid stair work and record one awkward landing measurement monthly for apprentice
Review existing household retirement plan annually against actual costs
Apply after 2036 only if wages needed to posted safe local part-time checking with gap-covering pay

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because Daniel's customers could spend less before robots interrupt my last site wages around 2031. Paid safe demonstrations and written local vacancies with actual hours and wages would help me choose sensibly. I prefer earning our way through a change, but an employer has to make learning possible during paid time.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You could ask how an apprentice knows a finished stair feels wrong. My knees can feel an uneven rise before my eyes find it. I want the apprentice to have that judgement as well as a password.

headlineQuote: My knees can feel an uneven rise before my eyes find it.
portrait: **Amira**, 58, is a skilled stair-fitting lead with a vocational certificate, higher pay and plenty of local builders.
She and **Daniel**, her partner, have grown children, a paid home and ten months saved; he repairs instruments.
She uses **AI daily**, enjoys new features and expects employers to provide paid learning and safe demonstrations.
Her **sixty-five target** stays conditional; rapid change threatens final wages, while ten years and strong resources support calm.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could weaken Daniel's customer income before 2031 robots interrupt her remaining stair wages.
whatWouldHelp: **Paid safe demonstrations** and written local vacancies with actual hours and wages would support sensible choices.
